title: Principal localization of a relative global complete intersection, with the presentation adding one variable
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n,c\ge0$ integers and $f_1,\dots,f_c\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] such that $T=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ is a relative global complete intersection [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection]. Let $h\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, let $g\in T$ be its image, and let $T_g$ be the localization of $T$ at $\{1,g,g^2,\dots\}$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Regard $f_1,\dots,f_c,h$ as elements of $R[x_1,\dots,x_{n+1}]$. Then $T'=R[x_1,\dots,x_{n+1}]/(f_1,\dots,f_c,hx_{n+1}-1)$ (with $n+1$ variables and $c+1$ equations) is a relative global complete intersection, and the $R$-algebra homomorphism $T'\to T_g$ with $x_i\mapsto(x_i\bmod(f))/1$ for $i\le n$ and $x_{n+1}\mapsto1/g$ is an isomorphism of $R$-algebras.

proof.text: (Part (a): the presentation $T'\cong T_g$.) Write $P=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and $P'=R[x_1,\dots,x_{n+1}]=P[y]$ with $y=x_{n+1}$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $I=(f_1,\dots,f_c)\subseteq P$, $\pi:P\to T$ the quotient map (so $\pi(h)=g$), and $I'=(f_1,\dots,f_c,hy-1)\subseteq P'$, so $T'=P'/I'$. Let $\beta:P'\to T_g$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] be the $R$-algebra homomorphism with $x_i\mapsto\pi(x_i)/1$ ($i\le n$) and $y\mapsto1/g$. The coefficientwise map $\pi[y]:P[y]\to T[y]$ is surjective with kernel $I\cdot P[y]=(f_1,\dots,f_c)P'$ by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-coefficient-map-kernel] (with $f=\pi$, one variable $y$, $\ker\pi=I$). By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-polynomial-quotient] (ring $T$, $r=g$), the $T$-algebra map $\lambda:T[y]\to T_g$, $y\mapsto1/g$, is surjective with kernel $(gy-1)T[y]$. The $R$-algebra maps $\beta$ and $\lambda\circ\pi[y]$ agree on $x_1,\dots,x_n,y$, so $\beta=\lambda\circ\pi[y]$, and $\beta$ is surjective. Kernel: $\pi[y](hy-1)=gy-1$, so $I'\subseteq\ker\beta$. Conversely, if $\beta(u)=0$ then $\pi[y](u)=(gy-1)v$ for some $v\in T[y]$; choose $v'\in P'$ with $\pi[y](v')=v$; then $\pi[y](u-(hy-1)v')=0$, so $u-(hy-1)v'\in(f_1,\dots,f_c)P'$ and $u\in I'$. Hence $\ker\beta=I'$ and $\beta$ induces an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $T'=P'/I'\xrightarrow{\sim}T_g$, which is the map of the statement ($x_i\mapsto(x_i\bmod(f))/1$, $x_{n+1}\mapsto1/g$). (Source: proof of 00SS (2), '$S_g\cong S[x_{n+1}]/(gx_{n+1}-1)$'; the same computation as the last sentence of the proof of 00SA.)

proof.text: (The fibre of $T$ and its presentation.) Fix a prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$, let $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $F=T\otimes_Rk$, the fibre ring [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Let $\rho:P\to k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] be the coefficient map along $R\to k$, $\bar f_j=\rho(f_j)$ and $\bar F=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_c)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension] (with $A=R$, the ring $k$, $J=\{1,\dots,n\}$) $P\otimes_Rk\cong k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, $a\otimes\mu\mapsto\mu\rho(a)$; by associativity of $\otimes$, $F=(P/I)\otimes_Rk\cong(P\otimes_Rk)\otimes_P(P/I)\cong k[x_1,\dots,x_n]\otimes_P(P/I)$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change] (with $A=P$, $B=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ via $\rho$, the ideal $I=(f_1,\dots,f_c)$) the latter is $\bar F$. So there is an isomorphism of $k$-algebras $\theta:F\xrightarrow{\sim}\bar F$, $\pi(a)\otimes\mu\mapsto\mu\rho(a)\bmod(\bar f)$; in particular $\theta(g\otimes1)=e$, the class of $\rho(h)$ in $\bar F$. (Source: the proof of 00SS (1), '$R'\otimes_RR[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)=R'[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$', with $R'=k$.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00SS (line 36640), proof of (1), lines 36660-36662

proof.text: (The fibre of $T'$ is a principal localization of the fibre of $T$.) Keep $\mathfrak p$, $k$, $F$, $\bar F$, $\theta$, $e$ of step 2. Applying $-\otimes_Rk$ to the $R$-algebra isomorphism $T'\cong T_g$ of step 1 gives a $k$-algebra isomorphism $T'\otimes_Rk\cong T_g\otimes_Rk$. By [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-localization-away-base-change] (with $A=T$, $B=k$ and the element $g$), $T_g\otimes_Rk\cong F_{g\otimes1}$ as $k$-algebras. The isomorphism $\theta$ carries $g\otimes1$ to $e$, hence induces an isomorphism of localizations $F_{g\otimes1}\cong\bar F_e$, $a/(g\otimes1)^m\mapsto\theta(a)/e^m$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] (it is well defined, bijective and multiplicative because $\theta$ is a ring isomorphism and the equality of fractions $a/s^m=b/s^l$ is defined by an equation in the ring). Composing, $T'\otimes_Rk\cong\bar F_e$ as rings; a ring isomorphism $\varphi$ induces a bijection $\mathfrak P\mapsto\varphi(\mathfrak P)$ of prime ideals preserving the closed sets $V(J)$, so $\operatorname{Spec}(T'\otimes_Rk)$ is homeomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}\bar F_e$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

proof.text: (The dimension of the localized fibre.) Keep the assumption $\bar F_e\neq0$ and let $X=\operatorname{Spec}\bar F_e$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. $X$ is nonempty: the nonzero ring $\bar F_e$ has a maximal ideal by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal], and a maximal ideal is prime. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open] (ii) (with $A=\bar F$, $f=e$), $\mathfrak P\mapsto\iota^{-1}(\mathfrak P)$ is a homeomorphism $u:X\to D(e)$ onto the open subspace $D(e)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}\bar F$. Let $x\in X$ and $y=u(x)$. For every open neighbourhood $V$ of $x$ in $X$, $u(V)$ is an open neighbourhood of $y$ in $D(e)$ and $u$ restricts to a homeomorphism $V\to u(V)$ of subspaces, so $\dim V=\dim u(V)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-homeomorphism-krull-dimension]; every open neighbourhood of $y$ in $D(e)$ is $u(V)$ for $V=u^{-1}$ of it. Taking minima [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point], $\dim_xX=\dim_yD(e)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace] (with $Y=\operatorname{Spec}\bar F$, $O=D(e)$), $\dim_yD(e)=\dim_y\operatorname{Spec}\bar F$, which is $n-c$ by step 4. So every point of the nonempty space $X$ has local dimension $n-c$, and [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions] gives $\dim X=\sup_{x\in X}\dim_xX=n-c$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. (Source: proof of 00SA, 'By the remarks following the definition $\dim(S_g)=n-c$'.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00SA (lemma-localize-lci, line 35852), proof, with the paragraph after Definition Tag 00S9 (lines 35834-35849)

proof.text: (Conclusion.) Let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ be a prime whose fibre ring $T'\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is nonzero. By step 3, $\operatorname{Spec}(T'\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))$ is homeomorphic to $X=\operatorname{Spec}\bar F_e$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-homeomorphism-krull-dimension] and step 5 its Krull dimension is $n-c=(n+1)-(c+1)$. As $T'=R[x_1,\dots,x_{n+1}]/(f_1,\dots,f_c,hx_{n+1}-1)$ has $n+1$ variables and $c+1$ equations, this says that $T'$ is a relative global complete intersection [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection]. Together with step 1 this is the statement. (If $c>n$, then $T=0$ by the definition, and steps 3-4 show that no fibre of $T'$ is nonzero: the argument covers this case.)

Six steps: (1) T' = T_g via the coefficient-map kernel and R[x]/(rx-1) = R_r leaves (route of the merged 00SA node, step 3); (2) the fibre F = T (x) k(p) is k[x]/(f-bar) (polynomial scalar extension, tensor-quotient base change); (3) T' (x) k(p) = F_g (algebra localization base change leaf); (4) a nonzero fibre of T' lies over a nonzero fibre of T, which is equidimensional of dimension n-c (equidimensional node); (5) dim of the nonzero principal localization is n-c (open immersion of D(e), dimension at a point on an open subspace, supremum of local dimensions); (6) conclusion with (n+1)-(c+1). No new nodes. Mathlib searches of the item (all three kinds, recorded at creation) suffice: no relative global complete intersection notion in Mathlib, not a leaf.
